body.model: NeuroMechFly v2 browser model from FlyGym v2.1.0

packet.zeroRule: Zero decoded neural evidence creates no active displacement. The unmodified upstream neutral position controls are an engineering posture condition, not tonic biological muscle force.
packet.gainRule: No normalized-population-activity to joint-angle gain is asserted by this artifact. The only absolute active transfer is the separately qualified adult front-leg resolved-spike to restrained-probe-equivalent joint torque; it is not generalized to other legs, unresolved units or extensors.
packet.timingRule: No gait phase, target pose, action sequence, collision response, or unobserved motor timing is introduced.

mapped.evidence: The BANC annotation names femur-tibia extension. A compiled-geometry finite perturbation shows that decreasing the MuJoCo pitch coordinate increases the anatomical angle between the proximal femur and distal tibia/tarsus vectors; the front-leg preparation defines increasing anatomical angle as extension.
mapped.amplitudeStatus: normalized activity unresolved; restrained front-leg resolved flexor spikes have a separate absolute torque bridge

mapped.evidence: The BANC annotation names femur-tibia flexion. A compiled-geometry finite perturbation shows that increasing the MuJoCo pitch coordinate decreases the anatomical angle between the proximal femur and distal tibia/tarsus vectors; the front-leg preparation defines decreasing anatomical angle as flexion.
mapped.amplitudeStatus: normalized activity unresolved; restrained front-leg resolved flexor spikes have a separate absolute torque bridge

torqueQualification.scope: adult front/prothoracic leg, restrained Azevedo force-probe preparation only
torqueQualification.inputEvidence: resolved slow or fast femur-tibia flexor spike counts and the frozen twitch/force curve in front-leg-spike-force-bridge-v1.json
torqueQualification.conversion: probe-equivalent force in micronewtons multiplied by the measured external 417 micrometre lever arm; 1 MuJoCo generalized torque unit in this millimetre-gram-second model equals 1 micronewton millimetre equals 1e-9 newton metre
torqueQualification.positionServoCondition: All 42 upstream position-actuator gain and bias parameters are set to zero during torque qualification; actuator force must remain exactly zero. Pinned passive joint stiffness, damping, contact and gravity remain active.
torqueQualification.zeroRule: Zero resolved spikes produce exactly zero applied generalized torque.
torqueQualification.runtimeStatus: explicit qualification interface only; not connected to the live motor packet or default body
unsupported: internal muscle origins, insertions, wrapping sites, tendon paths and moment arms
transfer from the measured front-leg preparation to middle, hind or contralateral legs

afferentQualification.runtimeStatus: explicit qualification vector only; not selected by the live whole-CNS world loop
physicalInputs: geometry-derived anatomical femur-tibia angle and angular velocity
raw local contact-force magnitude in micronewtons
applied joint torque in micronewton millimetres
afferentQualification.strainTransfer: disabled; contact force remains raw audit evidence because no source-supported force-to-campaniform gain is available
afferentQualification.claimBoundary: This closes physical joint motion and local contact into the existing FeCO/tactile-compatible qualification schema. It does not validate receptor gain, signed root identities, the high-frequency club carrier or live whole-CNS sensory closure.

roomQualification.runtimeStatus: explicit qualification profile only; the articulated body remains outside the live neural locomotor loop
roomQualification.coordinateRule: Room x and y are translated from top-left JSON coordinates to a frame centred on width/2 and height/2. The upstream neutral root offset is retained and spawn heading becomes a MuJoCo z-axis quaternion.
roomQualification.collisionFilter: Room colliders retain contype 0 / conaffinity 0 and the 55 pinned FlyGym ground-contact fly geoms retain their source collision masks. Every room collider receives an explicit MuJoCo contact pair with each of those 55 geoms. Fly self-collision and room-room collision remain disabled while the pinned explicit ground pairs remain unchanged.
roomQualification.contactSensors: The six leg-subtree sensors include ground and obstacle contacts in the derived room model. Contact force remains local audit evidence and no object identity, world coordinate, contact normal/tangent or room geometry enters the afferent vector.
roomQualification.parameterProvenance: The explicit-pair friction, solver and margin values match FlyGym v2.1.0 ContactParams defaults and the official browser game's obstacle pairs at the pinned source/browser commits. Matching an upstream engineering model is provenance, not material validation.
roomQualification.claimBoundary: The room file supplies measured-by-author 2-D dimensions and footprints only. Extrusion height, boundary thickness, explicit-pair friction/solver parameters and rigid/static behavior are frozen engineering assumptions, not biological or chamber-material measurements.

adhesionQualification.upstreamMechanism: FlyGym add_leg_adhesion creates one actively controlled normal-attraction actuator on tarsus5 per leg with control range 0 to 1.
adhesionQualification.browserGameBoundary: The official browser game has six additional adhesion actuators, but its baked controller writes 0 during swing and 1 during stance from CPG/preprogrammed step phase.
adhesionQualification.reasonDisabled: The pinned controller-free viewer body has only 42 position actuators and no adhesion actuators. Fly Umwelt has no experimentally justified BANC-to-adhesion command or biomechanical attachment/release rule, so it neither adds passive sticky feet nor imports gait-phase adhesion timing.
adhesionQualification.claimBoundary: Surface attachment remains unresolved until a defensible neural and biomechanical control bridge exists. Disabled adhesion is a preserved scientific limitation, not evidence that flies walk without adhesion.

structurallyInferred.reason: Joint identity and flexion/extension vocabulary make pitch the leading structural candidate, but the source annotation does not resolve the model coordinate convention or a control gain.
Joint identity and flexion/extension vocabulary make the only active tibia-tarsus pitch coordinate the leading candidate, but sign and population-to-angle gain lack a pinned experimental bridge.
The model mirrors the yaw axis between left and right legs and yaw is the leading protraction/retraction candidate, but the BANC labels do not establish the MuJoCo numeric sign or gain.

The model mirrors the roll axis between left and right legs and roll is a plausible abduction/adduction coordinate, but the compound posterior-lateral label and numeric sign require anatomical validation.

unresolved.reason: The flattened browser model has no explicit long-tendon actuator or pinned muscle-tendon routing that would justify distributing this channel across joints.
The source explicitly leaves the movement unknown; assigning a coordinate would invent anatomy.

unbridgedBodyCoordinates.reason: No stable BANC action label in the 72-channel packet uniquely identifies this coordinate.

claimBoundary: Only the femur-tibia antagonist pair is coordinate-mapped. Its corrected numeric sign is geometry-validated, but normalized population activity still has no angle or torque gain. A qualification-only front-leg path can apply already measured resolved-spike, restrained-probe-equivalent torque while the position servos are disabled. This is not an internal muscle/tendon model and is not transferred to other legs. Structurally inferred and unresolved channels never drive MuJoCo controls. A room-derived qualification model adds static boundaries, source-matched explicit wall/shelter contact pairs and local obstacle contacts without exposing room geometry to the CNS. Upstream passive mechanics, contact parameters, room extrusion, neutral posture and actively controlled adhesion remain model/engineering boundaries rather than validated fly physiology; adhesion is disabled because no neural timing bridge exists.
